key_concepts: Vertebrates are animals with backbones; invertebrates lack backbones
Vertebrates may be oviparous or viviparous
Mammals are warm-blooded, have hair or fur, and feed young with milk
Fish are cold-blooded, have scales, fins, and gills, and live in water
Birds are warm-blooded, have wings and beaks, and hatch from eggs
Amphibians have moist scaleless skin and live both in water and on land
Reptiles have dry scaly skin and hatch from eggs
Some birds have wings but cannot fly
Examples of vertebrate groups include dogs, fish, birds, frogs, and snakes
